A.why: Clearest bride from above with a flaring skirt and dark veil, but blocky sleeves square the shoulders and the tiered hem bands read armour-like.

B.why: Broad shoulders and a flat hem plate make a box on a tray, with a tabard front and no wisp colour.

C.why: Most fen-like with hanging willow strands and a reed crown, but the columnar skirt never flares and the set has no pale or glow.

D.why: Green banded hoops on the shoulders and a boxy skirt read as segmented armour, not a gown.

E.why: Best A-line flare in the run, spoiled by a skull-like back of the veil and flanged wide shoulders.

F.why: Truest palette with a readable wisp-blue hem, but no veil, wide green sleeves and a near-straight skirt.

notes: Every set still has square, blocky shoulders and too little flare, so none yet reads as a woman's outline first; the best parts are scattered (E's flare, F's palette and blue hem, C's willow strands, A's veil) and no one set combines them.
